body: tested, the output panel is using the smallest possible height by default which is too small:
Should be fixed now.

> Moves the buttons to the bottom, next to the filter.

How does it look when getting spammed errors/warnings at runtime? I worry going to 2, 3, 4 digits etc. will cause jumps which may be jarring (mainly 1->2 digits I guess).

Does it impact the min width of the Output dock / main viewport when on a tiny form factor?

setting min width on those to fit 2 digits should be fine, realistically the searchbar doesn't need to fit a lot of text

I'm also not sure why the copy button exists, everywhere else in the editor copying is only exposed via a context menu button and it seems to be enough

Yeah seems like Copy button can be removed.

> Does it impact the min width of the Output dock / main viewport when on a tiny form factor?

The editor can't get small enough to hit minimum size of the new Output bar, so for now it's not a problem. Although I didn't test with more digits.

This is the smallest I managed to shrink the Output: The filter box should probably have a minimum size, but it's unlikely someone will get it as little. Most often the minimum size of the editor is determined by the main screen buttons, or by the the toolbar (2D/3D/Script, Game seems to have the smallest width). EDIT: With HFlowContainer:

> Removes filter toggle (it's now always visible).

This PR made me realize I could've hidden it all along to give logs more vertical space, since I have never used it in my life. And now the vertical space is going to be permanently wasted...

Actually, I have a better argument to make. The button that I, personally, press the most in this panel is the "Clear" button. Right now its position is fixed within the panel and you can find it almost intuitively, regardless of the panel's size. With these changes the position of this button will be unpredictable, and changing with the severity level counters, as well as the flow container if that is implemented.

So, to me, the most important button in the panel will be harder to find and click, which is a usability regression. You could change the order and put it at the end of the row, but that would still be unreliable when used within the flow container. So there is that.

> With these changes the position of this button will be unpredictable

How exactly? The button is still going to be fixed in place.

> How exactly? The button is still going to be fixed in place.

Its position depends on the size of severity level buttons/counters. It's fixed relative to the right side of the filter box, but it's not fixed relative to the dimensions of the output panel itself.

I think the clear button is a bit inconvenient to click in both layouts because of how small it is, although in this PR incidentally it became a bit higher so it might be a bit less annoying to click despite the occasional horizontal shift from the numbers changing.

Overall though I press it a lot myself so I [opened a PR some time ago to make the shortcut for it actually usable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/89505), but I think it's still not enough and the shortcut needs to be a global editor shortcut that would work regardless of whether the panel is opened and that can be bound to something that's easier to press with left hand.
The counters could get some minimum size, so they are always the same up to e.g. 4 digits.

> The counters could get some minimum size, so they are always the same up to e.g. 4 digits.

We already discussed it here last year and I agree with @akien-mga that it's mostly imporant to eliminate the 1->2 digit jumps. Subsequent ones (2->3, 3->4, etc) likely happen too rarely to cause any real problem. So it probably should be 3 at most. Also if you're getting an error printed every frame you'll probably want to pause/stop the game first before clicking the clear button anyway.

> but I think it's still not enough and the shortcut needs to be a global editor shortcut that would work regardless of whether the panel is opened and that can be bound to something that's easier to press with left hand.

Yeah, I can never remember it nor do I find it comfortable to trigger. Of course I could change it on my end, but that should never be an argument against out-of-the-box usability IMO.

> Also if you're getting an error printed every frame you'll probably want to pause/stop the game first before clicking the clear button anyway.

Actually, in these situations I would often clear the output first, to make the editor more responsive for a moment. The output log is a performance hog, but it can handle a few thousand lines in rapid succession, but then gets progressively worse.
We can put the clean and copy icons on the far right. Can be a follow-up PR.

> Of course I could change it on my end, but that should never be an argument against out-of-the-box usability IMO.

I suspect the common usability path is to rely on `run/output/always_clear_output_on_play` which is enabled by default instead of manually clearing most of the time. It would be easier to tell how hot the button is if we had telemetry, but in my anecdotal case I suspect I clear the output more often than I actually need to out of my OCD :D

> Actually, in these situations I would often clear the output first, to make the editor more responsive for a moment. The output log is a performance hog, but it can handle a few thousand lines in rapid succession, but then gets progressively worse

Haven't had that personally but it sounds like godot could use virtual scroll or some other optimization for a lot of scrollable content. In the meantime maybe you could try reducing max lines with `run/output/max_lines`

> I suspect the common usability path is to rely on `run/output/always_clear_output_on_play` which is enabled by default instead of manually clearing most of the time.

Well, that's not the case that I'm talking about. I often clear the output during runs and in the editor, right before I test something, so I get an unencumbered log. Especially if I test something multiple times and don't want to get mixed up between stale and fresh results.

> Haven't had that personally but it sounds like godot could use virtual scroll or some other optimization for a lot of scrollable content.

It's because the log is a rich text label, and text shaping is expensive (in Godot at least). The more lines it has, the more expensive it gets, especially with additional formatting.

> We can put the clean and copy icons on the far right. Can be a follow-up PR.

If you put them on the right, they will be first to go when the flow container kicks in though. So that would be even worse. That's what I mention in my earlier comment.

Perhaps you have another suggestion?

Regardless, I don't think Yuri's issue with the position of the button is a blocker to this PR.

> Perhaps you have another suggestion?

I suppose the premise of your question is that this change here is inevitable and must happen? Then no, I don't have any suggestion. Now, if you were open to discussing merits of the change, then my suggestion would be "Keep it as is." I'd rather have more vertical space in the output log and buttons in predictable places than less vertical space and buttons that can move around.

The issue that the output panel cannot be reduced vertically beyond a certain size is notable. However, many other bottom panels (or really any docks now) already restrict minimum height of the bottom shelf. So I don't find that earned vertical space for the game view or 2D/3D viewports by allowing shorter output log will be in practice noticeable, outside of very specific scenarios.

Then there is a notion that a sidebar like this is a unique element for the Godot editor, which makes it standout in a bad way, somehow. And it's also not modern enough, somehow. I kind of reject the entire premise of such arguments. They are not based in user experience or usability/accessibility, but rather trends and familiarity from other tools. Maybe there should be more sidebars! After all, we have more horizontal space than vertical. And maybe other tools got it wrong because they don't work with their users when making changes.

I know, I know. I just rejected a user-created complaint one paragraph above. How hypocritical of me. Well, in truth I acknowledged it but considered that this change here ultimately doesn't yield the expected result, within the context of other editor GUI constraints. Thus I question the need for this change to address any actual withstanding usability problem. And thus when I bring up potential problems from this change my suggestion is: do not do it.

What if we could meet in the middle here? We can, potentially, do both:
- Move it to the bottom.
- Solve the moving buttons.

We could do this by making the button widths sufficient enough to hold 3 digits/characters, and when errors/warnings become >=100, switch over to a "99+" display. This would solve the variable width scenario no matter where the buttons are.


Personally, once you reach 3 digits of errors/warnings, I am not too sure how much more intel you get from the displayed number. 100+ becomes, "A lot". Normal (non-repeating) errors, I would think, are usually much less than 100 in number. The repeating ones are where you start getting the potential for width-based issues (And if they are repeating, I am okay seeing "99+" vs "15247"), but they are repeating... does one really care if it says "99+" vs "15247" when they are the same?

This solution only sacrifices space from the filter bar (Which I see as acceptable). I came to this idea since I actually agree with both sides:
- Moving them to the bottom is cleaner and sacrifices more "reasonably optional space".
- I never hide them, so I think having them visible all the time is a good thing.
- "Dancing" buttons (which are, by definition, intended to be interacted with) are jarring and I do think it potentially hurts usability.
- I also hit that clear button a lot.

You are talking about only 2 buttons... But there are 4 filter buttons actually 😄 And what makes sense for errors/warnings, may be not so applicable for standard print statements. For example 100+ print statements is not so much, and knowing exact number of print statements may be important.

> If you put them on the right, they will be first to go when the flow container kicks in 

... And clear button will stay on the same position in output dock if we will enable horizontal expand. So, that's exactly an issue?

...and "Clear" button will remain in the same position in the Output Dock if we enable horizontal expand for box container (if it's not already enabled). So what exactly is the problem?

> However, many other bottom panels (or really any docks now) already restrict minimum height of the bottom shelf.

That's a different issue, and I think it should be addressed separately. For example, I have several PRs to reduce the minimum size of various docks. Ultimately, this will allow us (at least I hope) to reduce the minimum editor window size, making it finally possible to use a normal horizontal "split screen" mode on a Full HD monitor.

I only included those two for less verbose typing of references to the buttons (I am on mobile). I, personally, am having a hard time thinking of a situation where knowing exactly how many there are (of any of them) solves a real problem. At 100+ you are almost definitely filtering them vs reading them one-by-one (I would hope).

In any case... why not include a tooltip when hovering the buttons that shows exact count (For those that need it)? Everyone wins, haha.
Anyway, this is something that could be improved in following PRs and letting people touch new output dock in next dev build to get more feedback will be not so bad idea, right?

Of course!

I was just dropping some ideas in here for potential solutions to status quo vs concerns while reading through. I saw this one in passing as I was digging through the 4.7 milestone, is all. Consider me a Godot Github Transient at this time, haha.
@PoshIndie Please don't take this personally, it was not directed at you personally, but at the discussion in general :)

Nothing taken personally! It is good to get counterpoints; It drives discussion and helps narrow to an optimal end result. I can honestly see pros and cons to both sides (I am mostly indifferent here).

(Likewise, my comments were directed at the general discussion/topic itself!)
Eh, any suggestions how to set minimum size to fit specified number of digits? I can't just hard-code it, because it depends on theme scale, font size, icon size, etc.

Valid question, and I lack a definitive answer to that one, as you are correct in the current context (Godot source code. I would need to dig in and investigate options) when it comes to "needs" to achieve it.

In the absence of anyone with more knowledge of Godot's source having a solution... it could be something to look into later.

I only have "general case" knowledge of how I achieved it in the past with similar things:
- Utilize a String with "WWWW" (4 in this specific case. "W" usually being one of the widest characters in Fonts). I guess it could be simplified as "Choose the widest character, get its width, and multiply that by 4". I also guess the character selection for necessary width is more limited (0-9 and +), so "W" was just "for example".
- "Get the width of the String" (This is kind of the "Finish the Owl" of the process, as if and/or how this can be/is achieved is very dependent on existing implementations/internal features determining viability (For instance, one would need to get the width of a character in the current font). I just do not have that level of intimate Godot source knowledge).

I keyed in on the "String width" as I would think the UI elements housing everything would adapt for UI Scale and such?

I could also be way off here, so I will leave it at that, haha.

@arkology 

> ...and "Clear" button will remain in the same position in the Output Dock if we enable horizontal expand for box container (if it's not already enabled).

Sure. Although shoving the most used (IMO) button into the furthest corner is kinda awkward. It feels to me that the usability is compromised just to make this particular change work, rather than usability being the goal of any change.


> That's a different issue, and I think it should be addressed separately.

Not at all. It's the big argument in favor of this change, to be able to reclaim vertical space by allowing shorter output log. I'm just putting it in the context of the entire editor UI. There remain bottom editors and docks which will take as much or more space. And there is a limit to how much you could even potentially reduce them before it becomes ridiculous and unusable.

I'm not sure what split screen mode you refer to, but assuming it's about showing the editor and the game (or code editor) side by side, reducing vertical size of bottom docks doesn't really help with that. Besides, why is that even a goal? Is that useful to a lot of people to shrink the editor so much? Like, I'm not saying it isn't, but this PR closes a 7 year old ticket for Godot 3.1, and you working on PRs isn't really a measure of public interest or practical need of many. No offense.

So I believe my original point stands. Though it has been ruled a non-blocker already, so ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

> Eh, any suggestions how to set minimum size to fit specified number of digits? I can't just hard-code it, because it depends on theme scale, font size, icon size, etc.

The cleanest solution would probably be outside of scope of this PR. You add 2 properties to the button (either via theme, or normally), one for the number of characters and another for the character itself. You then use the string of that character repeated that number of times as the minimum for the computed text size. That part is straightforward with TextLine.

That way, you only need the font and the font size, and don't hardcode anything other than the desired length.
